newsitem.title: CANADA: Starbucks union to hold off on walkout.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks union to hold off on walkout.

text.p: Unionized workers at Starbucks Corp in British Columbia plan to begin job action on Friday but will hold off on a full-fledged strike for now, a union official said Tuesday.
The 110 workers at eight coffee bars and a distribution center will be legally entitled to strike Friday morning, said Roger Crowther, a national representative for the Canadian Auto Workers union.
In an attempt to pressure the Seattle-based chain, the workers will begin wearing buttons that seek to raise customer awareness of their position.
"We are starting off with buttons...At this stage we are just trying to get them (Starbucks) to bargain in good faith," Crowther said.
Another move in the "un-strike" could include workers not dressing in accordance with the Starbucks dress code, he said. No pickets are currently planned.
Crowther declined to say how long such steps would continue before the union considered a walkout. The use of replacement workers is banned in British Columbia.

He accused Starbucks of refusing to negotiate and failing to make a counterproposal on wages. The union submitted a contract proposal late last week that the company rejected, saying the union had not changed its position substantially.
A Starbucks spokeswoman said earlier the talks were stalled and that it was up to the union to make the next move.
The union is trying to negotiate the first union contract at Starbucks, which has more than 1,000 outlets in North America.
The main issues in the negotiations are work flexibility and wages. The union is demanding a starting wage of C$10 an hour compared to C$7 currently.

Crowther said a labor board hearing over the union's complaint of unfair practices against Starbucks is slated for next week. The complaint revolves around Starbucks decision to close the Vancouver area distribution center.
